answer: Random peer audit stops bulk fake identities. A newcomer locks a 60-credit deposit and publishes a fingerprint of 20 tasks. Auditors check it against claimed work; a copied identity passes like a comet but leaves a mismatched trail, and failure forfeits the deposit. Fraud costs spiral: 100 fakes cost 100 x 60 = 6000 credits, above one shared reward. An honest agent pays once, passes, and climbs to the summit of work, earning undiluted rewards.
